title: A part's core has no row of its own on the Inventory or Part Library list
custom_preconds:
Setup (manual QA tester and Claude session)

Preconditions

  • You are signed in as an Admin at {Location-A} (for example Staging Heavy Duty - 9919); the Admin role has 'Part Library & Inventory → View', 'Part Library & Inventory → Create & Edit' and 'Part Library & Inventory → Delete' and can see costs and prices.
  • Parts → Inventory is open on the Active tab at {Location-A}.
  • Bin {Bin-A} is the default bin of {Location-A} (for example General Storage), the bin New Inventory Part fills in.
  • Inventory part {Part-A} (for example ZZAUTOTEST-PL-CORE-NOROW-01, described {Description-A}, for example ZZAUTOTEST PL CORE NO ROW) is active and tracked at {Location-A}, with 2 in {Bin-A} and a Core Charge of $25.00, so it has a core.
  • The core of {Part-A}, {Core-A}, is described "Core for {Description-A}".
  • A spreadsheet program or text editor is available to open the exported file.
custom_steps:
1. Type the part number of {Part-A} in the Inventory search.
  2. Read the rows listed.
  3. Replace the search text with Core for {Description-A}.
  4. Read the list.
  5. Type the part number of {Part-A} in the search again.
  6. Click the ⋮ actions menu and click Export.
  7. Open the exported file and read its part rows.
  8. Click the ⋮ actions menu and click Deactivate parts.
  9. Click the checkbox in the header of the list.
  10. Read the count in the bar.
  11. Click the X at the right end of the bar.
  12. Open Parts → Part Library and type the part number of {Part-A} in its search.
  13. Read the rows listed.
  14. Replace the search text with Core for {Description-A}.
  15. Read the list.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 2: Exactly one row is listed, {Part-A}, with $25.00 in its Core column; there is no second row for {Core-A}.
  • Step 4: No row is listed for "Core for {Description-A}"; the list shows its usual empty search result.
  • Step 7: The file holds one part row, {Part-A}; there is no row for {Core-A}.
  • Step 10: The bar reads 1 selected: the header checkbox ticked {Part-A} only, because {Core-A} has no row that could be ticked.
  • Step 11: The bar closes, the checkboxes go away and nothing was deactivated.
  • Step 13: One entry is listed, {Description-A}; there is no entry for "Core for {Description-A}".
  • Step 15: No entry is listed for "Core for {Description-A}".
  • Steps 1 to 15: A request made outside these screens that asks to change {Core-A}'s status on its own is refused with the reason "A core follows its part. Activate or deactivate the part instead."; no screen offers such a change, so this part cannot be checked by hand; write "not checked by hand" in the result comment.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-10647; story SV-10818 (Story 5, Change Tracking on an Existing Part); PRD "Parts Lifecycle Update", Confluence 829227015, v29 (14 Oct 2026 copy), S5-E3, with S1-R9b (Export follows the search), S2-R6 (the header checkbox) and §8 User Feedback Summary (A core asked to change status on its own), read 14 Oct 2026; Product's answer of 13 Oct (Chris Ward, question 6). Design: no board shows a core; boards 4.1 to 4.3 (actions menu, bulk mode) and 7.1 (Part Library), 13 Oct copy, unchanged on 14 Oct. Where cores show today: QA lead's answer of 9 Oct 2026, situation 5 (the Inventory Core column). Story SV-10818 (updated 9 Oct 2026) does not yet carry S5-E3; the PRD wins. Source-verified 14 October 2026; not yet build-verified (no Part Lifecycle QA build exists).

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S5-E3: “A core has no row of its own on the Inventory list, in Export or on the Part Library list, so it cannot be ticked for a bulk change. Its name (S13-R15) and its history show on the core's own Part History page. The core reason in S10-R13a applies when a core reaches a status change by any other route.”
  • S1-R9b: “The export includes every part on that tab that matches the current search, filters and Supply filter, including parts not yet scrolled into view. With nothing matching, the message "Empty export" shows and no file is made.”
  • S2-R6: “The checkbox in the header ticks or clears every row loaded in the list. The list loads 30 parts at a time as the user scrolls, so it ticks only the rows loaded so far. The count in the bar shows exactly how many parts will change.”
  • PRD §8 User Feedback Summary (A core asked to change status on its own): “"A core follows its part. Activate or deactivate the part instead." | Listed as the failure reason”
